job_application.reformulated_text:
A job applicant submits job applications to companies. The job applicant must regularly report the companies to which they submitted job applications. 

For each job application, a company confirms receipt and rates the application. The company and the job applicant can negotiate a job interview. If the company wants the job applicant to work for them, the job applicant enters the probation phase. 

During the probation phase, the job applicant can rate the company and the company can rate the job applicant. After the probation phase, the job applicant can rate the company and the company can rate the job applicant. 

If the job becomes permanent, the process ends, unless the job applicant rated the company C or less. If the job applicant rated the company C or less, the process continues, but the job applicant no longer has to report job applications.

maternity_leave.reformulated_text:
To support planning, taking, and extending a maternity leave, a process can be created with the following steps:

1. Fetch information about potential maternity leave models, including their duration in months and any split between parents.
2. Present the parent with a selection of these models to choose from.
3. Collect relevant information from the parent, such as their specific needs and requirements.
4. Notify the Social Security and the Company of the parent's intention to take maternity leave, ensuring timely notification.
5. Gather additional information from the Company regarding their maternity leave policies and procedures.
6. At the end of the maternity leave period, allow the parent to decide whether to extend their leave.

work_accident.reformulated_text:
To gather information about work accidents and almost work accidents, a process is created that involves the following steps:

An employee experiences an accident or almost an accident while performing insured gainful employment, which is considered a work accident if it occurs in a location, at a time, and with a cause that correlates to the insured employment. This includes accidents that occur while working from home, on the direct route from the permanent place of residence to work, to lunch, or on the way home, as well as accidents that occur during training sessions, doctor visits, childcare-related activities, or while using advocacy groups or professional associations.

For kindergarten children, schoolchildren, and students, an accident is considered a work accident if it occurs in a location, at a time, and with a cause that correlates to the school or university education or the compulsory kindergarten year that forms the basis of the insurance. This includes accidents that occur during school events, on the direct route from the child's place of residence to kindergarten or school, or while performing a practical task prescribed as part of the curriculum and/or the study regulations.

In an agricultural or forestry establishment, accidents can be considered work accidents if they do not occur directly while performing the insured employment, including working in the household of the owner, providing accommodation for guests, secondary occupations for selling agricultural products, building work for the establishment, and neighbourhood assistance for another establishment.

Certain accidents are considered the same as work accidents outside of professional activity, including activities under unemployment/labour market support services, assisting with an accident or donating blood, and training or serving as a member of a volunteer aid organisation.

The employee must inform the employer immediately of any work accident, any incident that would almost have led to an accident, any serious and immediate risk to safety and health that they discover, and any defect discovered in protection systems.

The employer must immediately report any work accident that leads to a fatality or serious injury to the Labour Inspectorate, if it has not been reported to the emergency services.

In addition, every work accident in which a person with accident insurance has been killed, or injured in such a way that they are unable to work for three days, in full or in part, must be reported to the responsible accident insurance provider within five days.

As a self-employed person, accidents involving people you employ and those that involve you must be reported to the accident insurance provider in good time.

Students and schoolchildren should report accidents to the competent directorate. Schools, educational facilities, and universities are obliged to report every work accident through which a person with accident insurance is physically injured or killed within a maximum of five days to the responsible accident insurance provider in triplicate.

In the case of private insurance, the insured party must report an accident in writing immediately in line with the conditions and to avoid the provider from being released from the obligation to perform. If there are fatalities, this must be reported within three days, even if the accident has already been reported.

employee: incident that would almost have led to an accident
serious and immediate risk to safety and health
employer: work accident leading to a fatality or serious injury
Labour Inspectorate: work accident leading to a fatality or serious injury
responsible accident insurance provider: work accident in which a person with accident insurance has been killed or injured in such a way that they are unable to work for three days
volunteer aid organisation: training or serving as a member

job_application.reformulated_text:
The process involves two main entities: the job application and the job applicant. A job application is created when the applicant submits an application to a company. The company must confirm receipt of the application and rate it. The applicant can negotiate a job interview. If the company wants the applicant to work for them, the applicant enters the probation phase. After the probation phase, the applicant can rate the company and the company can rate the applicant. The text does not specify what happens to the job application while the applicant is in the probation phase. 

The job application can progress to a permanent job, at which point the process ends, unless the applicant rated the company C or less. If the applicant rated the company C or less, the process does not end, but the text does not specify what happens to the job application or the applicant's reporting obligation.

evidence.entity_name: A job application is created when the applicant submits an application to a company. | The applicant can negotiate a job interview. | The applicant enters the probation phase. | The applicant can rate the company and the company can rate the applicant. | The applicant rated the company C or less.

maternity_leave.reformulated_text:
The process involves two entities: the leave and the parent. The process starts with the parent planning a maternity leave. The parent fetches information about potential leave models, which include the duration and split between parents. The parent then selects a leave model. 

The process then involves collecting relevant information from the parent. After that, the parent notifies Social Security and the company in time. The parent also gathers information from the company. 

At the end of the leave period, the parent decides about extending the leave. The text does not specify what happens if the parent decides not to extend the leave, nor what happens to the leave if the parent decides to extend it.

evidence.entity_name: The process involves two entities: the leave and the parent.

work_accident.reformulated_text:
The process involves several entities: the accident, the insured employment, the employer, the employee, the Labour Inspectorate, the accident insurance provider, and the competent directorate. 

An accident is considered a work accident under the following conditions: 
- it occurs in a location, at a time, and with a cause that correlates to the insured employment, 
- it occurs while working from home, 
- it occurs on the direct route from the permanent place of residence to work, to lunch, or on the way home, 
- it occurs during training sessions that serve to provide specific professional knowledge, 
- it occurs on the direct route from home, or from the workplace or training centre to a doctor and back, 
- it occurs on the way to or from the workplace or training centre with the purpose of taking a child to or collecting them from a childcare facility, a daycare facility, external care, or a school, 
- it occurs while making use of advocacy groups or professional associations, 
- it occurs in a location, at a time, and with a cause that correlates to the school or university education or the compulsory kindergarten year that forms the basis of the insurance, 
- it occurs while taking part in a school event or school-related event, 
- it occurs on the direct route from the child's place of residence or permanent accommodation to kindergarten or a school visit or on the way home, 
- it occurs while performing a practical task prescribed as part of the curriculum and/or the study regulations, 
- it occurs in certain professional (training) orientations, 
- it occurs in an agricultural or forestry establishment, but not directly while performing the insured employment, 
- it occurs while performing activities under unemployment/labour market support services, 
- it occurs while assisting with an accident or donating blood, 
- it occurs while training or serving as a member of a volunteer aid organisation.

The employee must inform the employer immediately of any work accident, any incident that would almost have led to an accident, any serious and immediate risk to safety and health that they discover, and any defect discovered in protection systems. 

The employer must immediately report any work accident that leads to a fatality or serious injury to the Labour Inspectorate, if it has not been reported to the emergency services. 

The accident insurance provider must be notified of every work accident in which a person with accident insurance has been killed, or injured in such a way that they are unable to work for three days, in full or in part, within five days. 

As a self-employed person, accidents involving people you employ and those that involve you must be reported to the accident insurance provider in good time. 

Students and schoolchildren should report accidents to the competent directorate. Schools, educational facilities, and universities are obliged to report every work accident through which a person with accident insurance is physically injured or killed within a maximum of five days to the responsible accident insurance provider in triplicate. 

In the case of private insurance, the insured party must report an accident in writing immediately in line with the conditions and to avoid the provider from being released from the obligation to perform. If there are fatalities, this must be reported within three days, even if the accident has already been reported.
